title: Introduce temporal tenant locks and KMS region ombudsman
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: Customers operating in regulated regions have asked for stronger guarantees that tenant-scoped KMS usage and residency assertions cannot be hijacked during operator interventions and rolling upgrades. This change introduces two complementary pieces: (1) a temporal tenant lock — a lightweight lease that pins a tenant's residency decision for a short, configurable window to avoid flip-flopping across concurrent operator actions, and (2) a KMS Region Ombudsman service that validates cross-service KMS binding proofs and emits a canonical 'residency-hash' that is included in audit envelopes for downstream correlation.

What this PR does (summary):
- Runtime: Add tenant temporal lock manager (pkg/tenantlock) that provides lease acquisition, renewal, and a small local cache to prevent thrash during rollout/upgrade. Leases are short-lived (default 30s) and are safe-to-expire — they are advisory and do not block normal operations if the ombudsman is unavailable.
- KMS: Introduce kms/ombudsman which queries configured KMS providers, verifies region-bound wrap/unwrap metadata, and publishes a signed residency-hash to the audit pipeline.
- RBAC: Policy compiler updates to attach an immutable operator-scope tag to requests that attempted forced region-change operations; the tag is surfaceable in RBAC v2 decision logs for later adjudication.
- Audit: Audit forwarder augmented to include residency-hash and tenant-lock context in canonical audit envelopes (compact JSON). Backwards-compatible: older consumers ignore extra fields.
- Installer/Private: Installer hooks to wire ombudsman address into private deployments and an opt-in flag for turning on strict residency-enforcement (default: off).

Files touched (high level):
- pkg/tenantlock/manager.go (new) — lease acquisition + LRU cache
- services/ombudsman/server.go (new) — verification endpoints and signer
- pkg/kms/provider_aws.go (mod) — attach region proof extraction
- pkg/policy/compiler/attach_tags.go (mod) — operator-scope tagging when policy detects forced overrides
- services/audit/forwarder.go (mod) — residency-hash injection
- charts/private/values.yaml (mod) — ombudsman opt-in flag and resources

Rollout and safety:
- Shadow rollout: ombudsman runs in shadow mode by default for the first week in Hosted and Dedicated; audit envelopes include residency-hash but policy is not enforced.
- Canaries: tenant-lock default lease is small and feature-flagged; we will enable it for a small set of tenants for 48h before broad flip.
- Fail-open behavior: if the ombudsman is unreachable, runtime operates normally and emits a "ombudsman_unavailable" indicator in the envelope; this preserves availability for latency-sensitive workloads.

Testing and verification:
- Unit tests for lease edge cases, provider proof parsing, and audit envelope format.
- Integration tests that run a local ombudsman, KMS emulator (wrap/unwrap metadata), and exercise the forwarder to ensure residency-hash is verifiable.
- E2E smoke test added to the installer acceptance suite to ensure flags are wired into private clusters.

Checklist:
- [x] design review with security and infra (SEC-482)
- [x] unit + integration tests added
- [x] installer hooks + chart changes
- [x] documentation: admin docs explaining lease semantics and ombudsman verification steps (docs/security/residency-ombudsman.md)

Related: ENG-2469 (design doc), SUP-1128 (customer report), previous work on residency proofs and audit envelopes.

Notes: This is intended to be low friction for customers — the ombudsman and lease are opt-in and default to conservative behavior. If we later decide to make strict residency enforcement mandatory for some compliance tiers, the ombudsman provides a canonical audit trail for that transition.

review_comments: Marco Ruiz (2025-01-11): Could we reduce the default lease to 15s? 30s seems long for some low-latency workloads. Also please add a prometheus metric for lease_acquire_latency.
Aisha Patel (2025-01-11): Reduced default to 20s after discussing tradeoffs; added lease_acquire_latency and lease_acquire_failures metrics. We'll watch canary 48h to decide further reduction.
Emily Chen (2025-01-12): How does this interact with Dedicated burst capacity routing? If a tenant migrates region temporarily due to capacity, will the tenant-lock block that?

Aisha Patel (2025-01-12): Tenant-lock is advisory and scoped to residency decision only. It does not block capacity-based routing; that path uses a separate capacity-grade routing token and ombudsman returns a different verification namespace. Added clarifying comment in compiler and docs.
Soren Jensen (2025-01-14): Integration tests flaky on CI: failed once on KMS emulator timeout. I recommend adding retry with jitter for the emulator in test harness.
Aisha Patel (2025-01-14): Added retries to test harness and bumped emulator timeout. Re-ran CI and green.
ci_checks: integration-e2e: pass (local KMS emulator with retries)
release_notes: Add opt-in temporal tenant locks (advisory leases) and a KMS Region Ombudsman that publishes residency-hash into audit envelopes. Shadow-mode rollout for Hosted/Dedicated; installer flag for Private. Backwards-compatible fields added to audit envelopes.
notes_for_ops: Enable ombudsman in shadow mode first. Monitor metric tenantlock.lease_acquire_latency and services.ombudsman.request_latency. Watch audit pipeline for residency-hash field and ombudsman_unavailable markers. If spike in ombudsman_unavailable, roll back ombudsman config and investigate KMS provider connectivity.
